turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. My son found out about a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of your class, and nobody called me first. Explain that.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student, and your own procedure says the same. So what else do you have, or is that it?
I don't need more proof than that.

"Don't need." Okay. Procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern, and 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in. Withdraw the zero, or I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." I'm writing that down. My child never lies, so are you calling him a liar, or me?
"Stands." Okay. Who decided that, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in the gradebook? If you can't answer, the principal can.
